scope: ET400 matched BT400/DT400 sampled frames 0,20,40,60,80; four known problem cases; not full-suite or continuous-motion approval

VP002.observation: ET restores visible wood grain, hand and natural warm color relative to BT. The sampled sequence does not demonstrate the requested bow bend; strip becomes very thin and then a bright broad flat shape. Fine-frame motion/geometry still requires checking.

VP004.observation: ET retains ruler markings and skin detail, unlike BT flat blue ruler. Late frames show large shiny irregular tearing/crumpling of the ruler rather than a convincing bend and propagating stress crack. Structural failure remains and looks worse than the largely unbent DT ruler.

VP009.observation: ET retains a visible worker, yellow helmet, glass and picture with more natural color than BT. The lifting tool/foreground becomes distorted ribbon-like black/silver geometry; valid suction-cup lifting is not established. Subject recovery does not mean the interaction is correct.

VP015.observation: ET reduces the pervasive BT blue cast and retains water reflection detail. A long boat-like dark shape, floating/irregular red elements and absent rower remain; the requested oar withdrawal/dripping process is not convincingly represented.

conclusion: Some natural colors, subjects and texture have recovered relative to BT, but these examples do not meet the joint visual/physical goal. Need complete main scores and existing feature-off/no-C/wrong controls before causal attribution. No additional version or sampler sweep is authorized.
